title: On-chip squeezed light in the audio frequency band
authors: Xuezhi Zhu, Yunyun Cao, Rui Liu, Yaya He, Fan Zhang, Yaqing Zhang, Shiwei Du, Meihong Wang, Xiaoshun Jiang, Xiaolong Su
abstract: Squeezed light in the audio-frequency band is a key resource for quantum metrology and quantum sensing. However, realizing stable audio-frequency squeezed light on integrated photonic platforms remains challenging due to technical noise and the difficulty of scalable phase referencing. Here, we demonstrate on-chip generation of audio-band two-mode squeezed states down to 60 Hz in a silica microcavity. To enable phase-stable operation without directly locking fragile quantum modes, we develop a coherent-comb control method in which a weak electro-optic reference comb co-propagates with the vacuum at the quantum frequency modes in an orthogonal polarization. This scheme provides quadrature measurement and long-timescale phase stability, thereby enabling covariance-matrix reconstruction. We verify the entanglement with the positive partial transposition criterion, which confirms inseparability via a minimum symplectic eigenvalue of 0.395 ($<0.5$). Our results establish an experimentally accessible route toward on-chip phase-stable audio-band squeezing and support the scalable framework for continuous-variable quantum information processing with integrated photonics.
summary: This paper reports the successful on-chip generation of two-mode squeezed light in the audio frequency band using a silica microcavity. To overcome technical noise and phase instability, the authors introduce a novel Coherent-Comb Control method. This technique enables stable, phase-referenced measurements, confirming both the presence of squeezing and entanglement, thus paving the way for integrated quantum sensing.
main_problem: The primary challenge is realizing stable, on-chip generation of squeezed light in the audio frequency band, which is difficult due to technical noise and the need for scalable phase referencing.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated on-chip generation of two-mode squeezed states down to 60 Hz and confirmed entanglement using the Positive Partial Transpose criterion.
method: They developed and implemented a Coherent-Comb Control (CCC) method, using a weak electro-optic reference comb co-propagating orthogonally to provide phase-stable quadrature measurement.
model_or_system: The experiment uses a silica microcavity where two-mode squeezed states are generated via Four-Wave Mixing (FWM) in a Kerr-nonlinear medium. The system is characterized by its ability to maintain phase stability over long timescales.
key_observables: Two-mode squeezing, entanglement (verified by minimum symplectic eigenvalue $\tilde{\nu}_- = 0.395$), and stable quadrature measurements.
important_parameters: Audio frequency band ($\ge 60$ Hz), reference power ($P_{ref} = 0.5$ mW), and the minimum symplectic eigenvalue threshold ($< 0.5$).
main_assumptions: The analysis excludes frequencies below 60 Hz due to classical/technical noise, and the method assumes the reference field does not introduce noise into the quantum signal.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the operating principle of the CCC method (co-propagating quantum and reference modes), device characterization, noise spectra dependence on reference power, and time-domain quadrature fluctuations confirming stable operation.
paper_structure: The paper details the physical challenge, introduces the CCC method for phase stabilization, presents the experimental setup and measurements (squeezing and entanglement verification), and concludes by establishing an accessible route for on-chip quantum processing.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the engineering hurdles—phase stability and noise mitigation—required to move continuous-variable quantum information processing from theory to scalable, integrated hardware platforms.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Operating principle of coherent-comb control (CCC) for phase-referenced homodyne detection of microcavity two-mode squeezed states. Paired quantum frequency modes Qi are generated via Kerr four-wave mixing, while a weak pump-derived electro-optic reference comb Ri co-propagates through the same optical path in an orthogonal polarization and with a fixed frequency bias ωb. After the cavity, the reference and quantum modes are separated and detected independently, so that phase sensing and feedback act on the reference path without introducing a bright locking tone at the quantum signal frequencies.

FIG. 2. Device characterization and experimental implementation. (a) Transmission spectrum of the selected pump mode at under-coupling conditions. (b) Transmission spectrum under overcoupling, exhibiting a pronounced non-Lorentzian (Fano- like) lineshape. (c) Comparison between chaotic microcombs generated above threshold and electro-optic (EO) combs used as the coherent reference. (d) Experimental setup implementing the pump-referenced phase-transfer scheme, including the EO- comb generation, polarization multiplexing, phase-locking, and balanced-homodyne detection. AOM, acousto-optic modulator; EDFA, erbium-doped fiber amplifier; PM, phase modulator; WDM, wavelength-division multiplexer;...

FIG. 3. Reference-induced measurement-noise characterization. (a) Noise spectra measured without the coherent reference for three conditions (uncoupled, coupled off resonance, and coupled on resonance), showing that no noise-floor elevation is resolved within the measurement setup. (b) Noise spectra measured with the coherent reference under different coupling/resonance conditions: uncoupled (Pref = 2 mW, before the microcavity), coupled off resonance (Pref = 2 mW), and coupled on resonance at Pref = 0.5 mW and 2 mW. The narrow features around 800–1000 Hz originate from oscilloscope oversampling of the control signal and do not reflect the optical noise floor.

FIG. 4. Phase-locked quadrature measurement, audio-band squeezing, and entanglement verification of the phase-stabilized two-mode squeezed state. (a) Representative time-domain quadrature fluctuations (anti-squeezed, SNL, and squeezed) recorded over a 100 s acquisition window with 10 kSa/s sampling rate after phase locking, showing stable access to different quadratures and stable locked operation during the measurement interval. (b) Frequency-domain squeezing and anti-squeezing spectra demonstrating observable squeezing down to the audio band. (c) Reconstructed covariance matrix. SNL, shot-noise level.
